verdict.rationale: Vue documents built-in provide/inject, including app-level app.provide for application-wide dependencies, which lets any descendant component reach shared values without a third-party library. The evidence does not explicitly present this as a global state-management pattern, and the official store options (Pinia, and Vuex in community posts) are separate packages rather than built-in primitives. Missing for 10: explicit docs on using reactive()/ref with provide or modules as a global store, guidance on mutations and devtools for built-in state sharing, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage global application state using built-in primitives without adding a third-party library

citations.quote: A parent component can serve as a dependency provider for all its descendants. Any component in the descendant tree, regardless of how deep it is, can inject dependencies provided by components up in its parent chain.
Truly reactive, compiler-optimized rendering system that rarely requires manual optimization.
